description: Defines the six core layers of the Operations Maturity System and the operational domains contained within each layer.

layers.name: Direction
layers.question: Where are we going?
layers.purpose: Translate strategic intent into clear operational direction.
weakSignals: Strategy exists as a slide deck, not as operating decisions.
Teams cannot explain how their work connects to a business outcome.
Priorities shift constantly with no visible tradeoff logic.
Different leaders describe the strategy differently.
strongSignals: Every team can trace its work back to a specific outcome.
Tradeoffs and constraints are explicit, not implied.
Priorities are stable enough to plan against, and change is communicated deliberately.
Risk appetite is stated, not discovered after something breaks.

layers.name: Design
layers.question: How should the organization work?
layers.purpose: Design the organizational architecture required to execute strategy.
weakSignals: The org chart describes reporting lines, not how work actually gets done.
Two teams both believe they own the same decision, or neither does.
Cross-functional work depends on personal relationships rather than defined interfaces.
Roles are titles, not accountabilities.
strongSignals: The operating model explains how capabilities combine to deliver outcomes.
Decision rights are explicit: who decides, who is consulted, who is informed.
Handoffs between functions are designed, not improvised.
Structure changes when the operating model changes, not the other way around.

layers.name: Execution
layers.question: How does work actually happen?
layers.purpose: Create repeatable systems through which work produces value.
weakSignals: Execution quality depends on who happens to be doing the work.
SOPs exist but nobody follows them, or nobody remembers they exist.
Handoffs lose information, context, or accountability.
Escalation is the default way problems get resolved.
strongSignals: Processes are documented, owned, and consistently followed.
Standards and controls catch problems before they reach the customer.
Automation removes manual toil from stable, well-understood processes.
Handoffs are explicit, with clear inputs, outputs, and owners.

layers.name: Management
layers.question: How do we run the system every day?
layers.purpose: Create the mechanisms that actively manage execution.
layers.highlight: Processes don’t run organizations. Management systems run processes.
weakSignals: Meetings happen on schedule but no decisions come out of them.
Capacity is invisible until something is already late.
Issues are managed reactively, one fire at a time.
Change lands on teams with no plan for absorbing it.
strongSignals: Operating rhythms exist to make and track decisions, not just to meet.
Capacity and demand are visible and actively balanced.
Risks and issues are tracked to resolution, not just discussed.
Change is sequenced against the team's actual capacity to absorb it.

layers.name: Intelligence
layers.question: How do we know what's happening?
layers.purpose: Turn operational activity into reliable information and decisions.
weakSignals: Dashboards exist but nobody changes a decision based on them.
Metrics are lagging only, so problems are visible after they've already hurt customers.
Different teams report different numbers for the same thing.
Data quality issues are common knowledge but never fixed.
strongSignals: Every core metric connects to a decision someone actually makes.
Leading indicators surface problems before they become customer-facing.
Metrics are trusted enough that people argue about the response, not the number.
Operational health is monitored continuously, not reconstructed after a failure.

layers.name: Evolution
layers.question: How does the organization become better?
layers.purpose: Create an operating system capable of learning and adapting.
weakSignals: The same problems recur because only symptoms get treated.
Improvement happens in bursts, driven by whoever is frustrated this quarter.
Lessons learned are not captured, so mistakes repeat across teams.
New tools and automation get layered onto broken processes.
strongSignals: Root cause analysis is routine, not reserved for major incidents.
Improvement is continuous, measured against an established baseline.
Knowledge is captured and reused, not trapped in individual heads.
The organization treats its operating system as something it deliberately evolves.
